findings.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:54-77 — A single try/catch wraps the entire cancel loop and the batched DB deletes; one failing SendGrid request (invalid/already-consumed batch_id, 429, network error) aborts all remaining cancellations and skips every row deletion, and since the failing reminder row is never removed it is retried and fails on every subsequent cron run, permanently blocking cancellation/cleanup for all other cancelled reminders.

[Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-52 — The `remindersToCancel` query has no `scheduledDate` lower bound and no `scheduled: true` / non-null `referenceId` guards, so reminders whose send time has already passed (booking cancelled after the reminder fired, or after cron downtime) get cancel requests that can error at SendGrid, triggering the all-or-nothing failure.

[Medium/concurrency] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:214-229 (with handleCancelBooking.ts:484-492) — Cancelling at SendGrid is deferred to the cron's final-hour window, so correctness depends on the cron running at ≤1h cadence with no missed runs (deploys, restarts, self-hosted deployments without the cron configured); otherwise reminders for cancelled bookings are still delivered, whereas previously cancellation was initiated directly in the cancel flow.

[Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:962-975 — The original booking's reminders are cancelled (irreversibly at SendGrid, unawaited) before the reschedule is committed; if `eventManager.reschedule` or any later step throws, the still-active original booking permanently loses its reminders with no rollback.

[Low/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:962-967 — The try/catch wraps a forEach invoking async functions without await, so it can never catch their errors; the `log.error("Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders")` handler is unreachable dead code.

[Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:484-492 (same pattern in viewer/bookings.tsx:484-492 and viewer/workflows.tsx:211, 375, 517, 572) — Reminder cancellation/deletion is now fire-and-forget; previously the DB deletions were awaited via `Promise.all` before responding. With errors swallowed inside the managers, failures are invisible, and in serverless environments unawaited post-request work may never complete, leaving cancelled bookings with live reminders.

[Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:178-186 (same class of issue in emailReminderManager.ts immediateDelete branch) — On Twilio/SendGrid failure the error is swallowed and the DB row is left scheduled with no `cancelled` marker (the SMS path never sets one at all), so there is no retry path and the SMS/email still fires for a cancelled or rescheduled booking.

[Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:485-490 — The reschedule path uses the deferred email cancellation (no `immediateDelete` flag) while the equivalent reschedule logic in handleNewBooking.ts:966 passes `true`; the old scheduled send stays live at SendGrid until the cron window, an inconsistency that looks like a missed flag rather than intended behavior.

[Low/data] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:206-212 — The `immediateDelete` branch cancels at SendGrid but never deletes the DB row; in the reschedule flow nothing else removes the original booking's WorkflowReminder rows (workflows.tsx callers are covered by cascade deletes, this path is not), so orphaned rows accumulate.

[Low/data] packages/prisma/schema.prisma:644 — New `cancelled Boolean?` column is nullable with no default; existing and newly created rows get NULL, which won't match `cancelled: false` filters in future queries. Should be `Boolean @default(false)` (NOT NULL).

[Medium/test_gap] No tests added for the new deferred-cancellation lifecycle — cron cancel loop, cancel/reschedule flows, `cancelled` flag handling, or the changed `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` signatures — despite this being regression-prone logic.

[Low/doc_defect] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:901-963 — ~60 lines inside the SMS preview block are re-indented with no logical change, adding diff noise, obscuring review, and breaking git blame for that section.

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:54-77 — A single try/catch wraps the entire cancel loop and the batched DB deletes; one failing SendGrid request (invalid/already-consumed batch_id, 429, network error) aborts all remaining cancellations and skips every row deletion, and since the failing reminder row is never removed it is retried and fails on every subsequent cron run, permanently blocking cancellation/cleanup for all other cancelled reminders.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation logic wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop and the subsequent `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` in a single `try/catch`. If `await client.request(...)` throws for any one reminder, execution jumps to `catch`, aborting the rest of the loop and skipping `Promise.all`, so already-queued deletes are never executed and later reminders are not processed. The failing row is also never deleted/updated, so it will be retried on future runs and can repeatedly prevent cleanup depending on result ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-52 — The `remindersToCancel` query has no `scheduledDate` lower bound and no `scheduled: true` / non-null `referenceId` guards, so reminders whose send time has already passed (booking cancelled after the reminder fired, or after cron downtime) get cancel requests that can error at SendGrid, triggering the all-or-nothing failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new `remindersToCancel` query selects any `workflowReminder` with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`, with no `scheduled: true` filter and no `referenceId` non-null guard. The subsequent loop always issues a SendGrid cancel request using `batch_id: reminder.referenceId`, so reminders with `referenceId` null/invalid (or already-sent reminders with past `scheduledDate`) can trigger a SendGrid error. Because the loop `await`s each request inside a single `try`, one failure aborts processing of remaining reminders and skips the deletion `Promise.all`, matching the “all-or-nothing” failure concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:214-229 (with handleCancelBooking.ts:484-492) — Cancelling at SendGrid is deferred to the cron's final-hour window, so correctness depends on the cron running at ≤1h cadence with no missed runs (deploys, restarts, self-hosted deployments without the cron configured); otherwise reminders for cancelled bookings are still delivered, whereas previously cancellation was initiated directly in the cancel flow.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes email reminder cancellation semantics: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` now *does not* cancel at SendGrid for the common call sites (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts` and bookings/workflows routers call it without `immediateDelete`), and instead only marks the DB row `cancelled: true` via `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)`. Actual SendGrid cancellation + DB deletion is moved to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only processes `cancelled: true` reminders with `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. This creates a real reliability/ops dependency on that scheduler running frequently enough; the finding’s concern is grounded, but whether it’s a “bug” depends on deployment guarantees about that cron/API being invoked, which isn’t verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, inside `if (originalRescheduledBooking?.uid)`, the code cancels/deletes `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders` *before* calling `eventManager.reschedule(...)`. Those cancellations are async but invoked via `forEach` without `await`, and they can be irreversible (e.g., `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)` issues a SendGrid cancel request and returns; `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` cancels Twilio and deletes the DB row). If `eventManager.reschedule` (or later steps) throws, the original booking can remain effectively active while its reminders have already been cancelled/deleted, with no rollback shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:178-186 (same class of issue in emailReminderManager.ts immediateDelete branch) — On Twilio/SendGrid failure the error is swallowed and the DB row is left scheduled with no `cancelled` marker (the SMS path never sets one at all), so there is no retry path and the SMS/email still fires for a cancelled or rescheduled booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `smsReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` wraps both `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and the Prisma `workflowReminder.delete` in a single `try`/`catch`. If Twilio cancellation throws, the catch only logs and returns, so the DB row is not deleted and is not marked `cancelled` (SMS path never sets `cancelled` at all). Similarly in `emailReminderManager.ts`, the `immediateDelete` branch issues the SendGrid cancel request and then `return`s without updating/deleting the DB row; if the cancel request fails, the error is swallowed and the row is left unchanged (no `cancelled` marker), leaving no retry signal while the external send may still occur. This is directly visible in the diff changes to both delete functions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:485-490 — The reschedule path uses the deferred email cancellation (no `immediateDelete` flag) while the equivalent reschedule logic in handleNewBooking.ts:966 passes `true`; the old scheduled send stays live at SendGrid until the cron window, an inconsistency that looks like a missed flag rather than intended behavior.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in the diff: in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (reschedule flow), email reminders are cancelled via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` with no `immediateDelete` flag. In `emailReminderManager.ts`, when `referenceId` exists and `immediateDelete` is not set, the function only marks the DB row `cancelled: true` and does not call SendGrid to cancel the scheduled send. By contrast, `handleNewBooking.ts` reschedule cleanup calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`, which does issue the SendGrid cancel request immediately. This inconsistency means the TRPC reschedule path can leave the SendGrid scheduled send active until later processing, which can result in unintended sends compared to the other reschedule path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:206-212 — The `immediateDelete` branch cancels at SendGrid but never deletes the DB row; in the reschedule flow nothing else removes the original booking's WorkflowReminder rows (workflows.tsx callers are covered by cascade deletes, this path is not), so orphaned rows accumulate.

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` returns early in the `immediateDelete` branch after canceling the SendGrid batch, without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row or even marking it `cancelled` (unlike the non-immediate branch which sets `cancelled: true`). The diff shows the reschedule path in `handleNewBooking.ts` calling `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` for `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders` and not performing any Prisma delete afterwards (the prior pattern of collecting `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)` promises was removed elsewhere). So those reminders can remain in the DB indefinitely and will not be picked up by `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`'s cleanup (it only targets `cancelled: true`).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial, regression-prone lifecycle changes without any accompanying test additions in the shown changes: (1) `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` signatures and semantics change (now take `reminderId`, may set `cancelled` or delete depending on args) in `emailReminderManager.ts` / `smsReminderManager.ts`; (2) cancellation flows in `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `handleNewBooking.ts`, and multiple TRPC workflow/booking routes are updated to call the new signatures and no longer directly `deleteMany` reminders; (3) a new deferred cancellation loop is added in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` that finds `WorkflowReminder` rows with `cancelled: true` and deletes them after calling the provider; (4) a new `cancelled` column is added to the Prisma model/migration. No test files or test updates appear in the diff to cover these new paths/flags/cron behavior, making the finding specific and diff-grounded.
